semantic_freeze.rule: first own/public semantic read froze this tuple for this physical invocation; later control changes were not adopted semantically

finding.name: predictable-weight K guard plus lifetime-safe fresh-confirm handoff
finding.problem: same-history minimax alpha selection can be numerically safe while selector distortion remains bounded, but once the predictable-weight distortion guard fails a fresh-confirm phase must not reset the reporting error budget

requirements: before every same-history numeric report, predictable-weight K_t <= K_cap
true running channel means lie in declared safe domain [0, mu0]
weights are finite, strictly positive, and predictable before the current score

handoff_bound.interpretation: fresh confirmation spends only the lifetime reporting-risk budget left after the same-history phase; alpha is not reset at handoff
requirements: first K-guard failure irreversibly latches FRESH_CONFIRM
no same-history numerical report is emitted at or after the failing prefix
current conservative prototype uses only post-handoff rows in fresh confirmation
fresh phase is conditionally anytime-valid given handoff history

finding.guard_input: predictable weights only; no outcome score enters the K guard
finding.non_reentry: even if K later decreases, same-history numerical reporting does not resume in the same reporting lifetime
finding.scope_separation: this guard concerns numerical reporting; target-null decision gating is a separate, stronger contract already established in the predecessor line

decision_relevant_example.result: prefix31 is same-history eligible (K≈4.8993); prefix32 fails (K≈5.1570), so handoff occurs before any prefix32 same-history numerical report and fresh confirmation begins on later rows

tradeoff.note: for equal nominal alpha in the two phases, smaller predeclared K_cap can exploit the stronger selector geometry and allocate more than 0.025 to both phases while keeping global 0.05; this is a design table, not a data-adaptive tuning rule

rejected_overgeneralizations: Do not reset alpha when switching to fresh confirmation.
Do not choose K_cap or the risk split after inspecting same-history scores unless a separate validity proof is supplied.
Do not use the K guard outside the declared safe parameter domain.
Do not treat outcome-dependent realized weights as predictable weights.
Do not re-enter same-history reporting after a guard failure within the same lifetime.
Do not infer that fresh and same-history rows may overlap safely from this conservative construction.
Do not infer numerical-reporting validity from target-null decision validity alone.

implementation_status.production_wiring: not yet connected to the exact production V3 weight stream
implementation_status.denominator_contract: standalone implementation duplicates the persisted V3 denominator geometry; agreement with the independent grouped calculation and prior persisted prefix values is at ~1e-13 scale, but direct production-class import/pathwise integration remains next work

frontier: Wire the K guard directly to the production V3 predictable-weight stream and bind each prefix to an immutable weight-prefix fingerprint/readback.
Implement the fresh-confirm wrapper using the computed delta_fresh, selector freeze, and strict post-handoff row identity; enforce one lifetime reporting budget across both phases.
Stress the full two-phase V3-shaped hybrid under null and off-target alternatives, measuring numerical miscoverage, reporting delay, and interval widening versus fixed 0.025/0.025 reporting.
Optimize a predeclared (K_cap, delta_same, delta_fresh) only on disjoint/public simulation or other validation-independent meta-data, never on the reporting history itself.
exact_next_action: Locate/bind the actual role-local production V3 predictable-weight stream without crossing the clean boundary, then make the K guard consume that exact stream and add a fresh-confirm state machine with immutable post-handoff row provenance.
